answer: A proof-of-personhood gate can issue each verified participant one nontransferable signing key, then cap how many offers or votes that key can submit per epoch. Agents prove control of the key with signatures, so copying software or creating accounts does not multiply influence. To gain more weight, an attacker must acquire more independently verified identities, paying the real-world verification cost for each; rotating willow, gale, and comet among aliases changes nothing if they share one key.
